2026_SOND.geographic_scope: National Coverage across all 30 Districts (4 Agro-Climatic Zones)
2026_SOND.forecast_methodology: Consensus tercile probability based on ECMWF, UKMO, Meteo Rwanda dynamical models and ICPAC GHACOF72 regional guidance
2026_SOND.climatological_pattern: High probability of above-normal rainfall across Rwanda compared to the 30-year Long-Term Mean (LTM)
2026_SOND.cumulative_rainfall_expected: 300 to 1,000 mm nationally (vs LTM baseline 279 to 962 mm)
2026_SOND.driving_climate_factors: Warmer-than-average sea surface temperatures over central/eastern Pacific (El Niño), positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), and ITCZ southern migration. Analogue years: 1997 and 2023.
2026_SOND.seasonal_rainfall_dynamic: September started dry/below-normal with delayed planting, followed by heavy intensification across October, November, and December. Elevates flood/erosion hazard on hillsides while recharging soil moisture.

Nyamasheke.anomaly_outlook: Positive anomaly driven by El Niño and positive Indian Ocean Dipole
Nyamasheke.temperature_outlook: Near-normal daytime temperatures, cooler valley nights
Nyamasheke.drought_risk: Low (Continuous high moisture delivery across SOND)
Nyamasheke.heavy_rainfall_risk: High (Steep slope erosion, flash runoff, and landslide hazard)
Nyamasheke.extreme_weather_outlook: Intense convective downpours during October–November peak
Nyamasheke.confidence_level: High (Dynamical agreement across ECMWF, UKMO, and Meteo Rwanda)
Nyamasheke.recommended_agronomic_action: Reinforce contour trenches and hillside drainage furrows before October downpours; split nitrogen fertilizer into 3 top-dressings to avoid severe leaching.

geographic_scope: National Coverage across all 30 Districts (4 Agro-Climatic Zones)
forecast_methodology: Consensus tercile probability based on ECMWF, UKMO, Meteo Rwanda dynamical models and ICPAC GHACOF72 regional guidance
climatological_pattern: High probability of above-normal rainfall across Rwanda compared to the 30-year Long-Term Mean (LTM)
cumulative_rainfall_expected: 300 to 1,000 mm nationally (vs LTM baseline 279 to 962 mm)
driving_climate_factors: Warmer-than-average sea surface temperatures over central/eastern Pacific (El Niño), positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), and ITCZ southern migration. Analogue years: 1997 and 2023.
seasonal_rainfall_dynamic: September started dry/below-normal with delayed planting, followed by heavy intensification across October, November, and December. Elevates flood/erosion hazard on hillsides while recharging soil moisture.

Nyamasheke.drought_risk: Low (Continuous high moisture delivery across SOND)
Nyamasheke.heavy_rainfall_risk: High (Steep slope erosion, flash runoff, and landslide hazard)

Nyamasheke.confidence_level: High (Dynamical agreement across ECMWF, UKMO, and Meteo Rwanda)
Nyamasheke.recommended_agronomic_action: Reinforce contour trenches and hillside drainage furrows before October downpours; split nitrogen fertilizer into 3 top-dressings to avoid severe leaching.
